My recent work examines how visual attention supports social perception. Using eye tracking and behavioral tasks, I study how people explore faces over time, how accurately they judge gaze direction, and how these processes relate to the ability to infer other people's mental states. I am particularly interested in how the timing and organization of visual exploration help explain individual differences in social understanding.
